questions.question: What is a sample space $S$ for a random experiment?
options: The set of all possible outcomes in the chosen model
A single outcome that actually occurs
The probability assigned to one event
A rule for averaging numerical outcomes, for every possible choice of input.
questions.explanation: The sample space $S$ of a random experiment is the set of all possible outcomes in the chosen model.
questions.source_support: The definition says that the sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of the experiment.
option_explanations: A single outcome that actually occurs is the realized result, not the whole set of possibilities.
The probability assigned to one event is a number, not the set of outcomes.
A rule for averaging is an expectation rule, not the sample space.

questions.explanation: The sample space is the universe of all possible results in the model; every event is a subset of it.
